what: Tiling cabinet base with brass feet
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: source artwork for a vertically tiling cabinet, to be cut into a crown, one repeated shelf row, and a base.
Input images: Image 1 is design/art/style-sheet.png, the approved style reference: match this style exactly. Image 2 is design/art/shelf.png, the existing shelf reference: same wood, brass and line style as this shelf.
Create one tall, straight-on front-view wooden cabinet with a slight top-down angle showing the top surface of each board, like Image 2. Warm brown wood posts at the same x positions from top to bottom, brass ball finials above, brass brackets at the far left and right of each board, brass feet below. A continuous opaque cream #F3E2BB wallpaper or light-wood back panel fills between the posts, with very subtle paper grain. Outside the posts is fully transparent. The cabinet is empty: no vessels, plaques, text or symbols.
Composition: portrait image, cabinet fills nearly all canvas width. Left post outer edge about 2.3% and inner edge about 9.4% of width; right inner edge about 90.6% and outer edge about 97.7%. Three identical shelf bays with evenly spaced boards; each bay is tall enough for a vessel above the board. Board front faces are plain, about 52 px high after scaling to 1024 px wide. Board tops are visible, standing surfaces flat and horizontal. Keep central horizontal region x 17.2%-82.8% very plain and uniform at every x: horizontal wood grain on boards; flat back panel with fine grain only; no knots, vertical grooves, brackets or localized light spots. Put all hardware outside that region. At every horizontal cut through the posts and back panel, their width, color, and shading stay continuous. Avoid perspective taper; all boards are level and full width.
The final tiles will be composited with three or five vessels on each shelf, so leave the bays empty and spacious.
The view instruction here replaces the three-quarter view and square-canvas instruction below for this cabinet only. Keep every other part of the style block unchanged.

Match the attached style sheet exactly.

Draw a single assembled, closed collectible souvenir miniature loosely inspired by Taipei's historic North Gate (Cheng'en Gate). The attached image is the style reference. Architectural cues observed in the real photo: broad squat blue-gray ashlar base, one deep semicircular arch with sturdy rectangular piers, wax-red rectangular upper wall with two tiny dark square openings and a central oculus, one swept single-eave tiled roof with a raised central ridge and restrained upturned corners. Use wax-red/plum roof tiles and a small brass or cream ridge highlight. Simple readable shapes at 40 px, predominantly frontal with a little of the right side visible. One continuous eave separates the detachable tile roof from the wall with a clear seam; the miniature is still closed and there is no rolled paper visible yet. The arch is dark with a recessed back wall in the closed state. No plaque or plaque outlines, no lettering or glyphs, flags, finial symbols or emblems. No environment, floor, shadow outside silhouette or extra objects. Set the object about 70% of square canvas width and height, horizontally centered, base close to 88% down and clear space above the ridge for lifting.
postprocess: One shared Lanczos 1254 to 1003 resize and (16, 7) canvas offset. Discard alpha below 20. Closed pixels divided between base and roof by the edited roof mask. Crop and feather the edited open recess and letter into a separate reveal layer.

Approved regional palette exception for this durian: muted natural food colours, specifically desaturated leafy olive-green and tea-brown for the husk and stem, egg-yellow and rice-white for the fruit. Ink lines stay plum or navy.
Draw one whole closed durian as a hand-inked collectible vessel, the fruit itself that inspired the nickname of Singapore’s Esplanade. One broadly oval fruit with a gently tapered lower tip, upright and slightly tilted, a short woody stem centered near the top. Fairly large, distinct green pyramidal thorns with selected brass-tinted sunlit tips. postprocess: All edits use the shared uniform downscale and offset. The seam partitions the original exterior for the exact closed stack. The generated pale pith strips are registered to the same seam and revealed with the split. The complete pods and letter are one reveal layer.
